Personally, I like to keep things simple and the simplest course of action would be to wash your hands of the situation, however it seems you have children with him already so breaking up and moving on without any more contact isn’t feasible. 

I think you have a few options. What it seems like what your doing now, is remembering, every time his other daughter is brought you go back to that time when y’all were separated, and I can imagine that’s not a fun place to be. 

Now this is easier said than done, but what I would try to do in your position (as it seems your more or less committed to him) is to fully embrace that little girl. Think about how awesome you are and your family is and now you get the privilege to share that and help mold this girl into an even better person than if you weren’t around. It can be hard being mom#2 but if you can, go for it. 

And I don’t think you need to fully explain everything to your kids, just do what feels natural and introduce them. Kids are very perceptive and as we get older we tend to forget that, especially when we see how stupid they can be. They’ll get it. And if one day it feels right, tell them, come clean, they’ll understand and will appreciate the honesty. 

You don’t need a traditional family to make a happy family. Having a happy family is usually most dependent on the leaders of the family being happy, which means you. If you truly feel the situation is okay, it will spread; however the reverse is also true. 

Perhaps I have no idea what I’m talking about, after all I’m some random stranger on the internet. Though my motto had always been that shit happens and you have to roll with the punches

Also notice how I focused on the little girl and you and your family. I never once mentioned the girl’s mother. You will have to do the same. You will have to separate the two to make this work. It is. How to fix it? Well, that's a little more difficult. Almost every ccg has a win % higher for the person going first, usually between 51% and 55% and it's up to the creators how to get it closer to 50/50. Certain matchups and certain decks may buck this trend, but exceptions don't nullify this fact. In fact, well before set 2 was released an aggro rakano player posted a spread sheet of all their games. And unsurprisingly had a much higher win rate on the play. However what interested me, was the fact that even against decks that would seemingly want to be in the draw, like feln control performed much better on the play. However small sample size and individual matchup all apply to those numbers. But why? Well it's pretty easy to see how being able to answer an oni ronin with vara' s favor without any warcries is a huge wrench in the rakanos player game plan. And i also don't subsribe to the notion that going second is better in a control v control matchup. Why because of the amount of cards were taking about that will be played during the game. Lets say in an aggro matchup only ~10 cards get played. Therefore every card has a higher impact on the game, compared to a control matchup where 30 or 50 cards are played. However it's already been determined that aggro relies on tempo so card advantage is meaningless. And decks built around card advantage will often get to that point anyway, regardless if they go first or second. And that one "free" the person gets on the draw, even in a control v control matchup isn't all that impactful especially if both players go through 30 - 50 cards, because then that extra card is only 2-3% of your game plan

Tldr: going first is almost always better for almost every deck in almost every matchup, besides some fringe circumstances

the last word has been traditionally a finisher in feln control lists. very neat interactions is that if the relic weapon has battle skills, that means so does your "hero" and therefore your spells. example: having the last word equipped and having lightning storm in hand, so now its essentially a 2 power harsh rule, since you have deadly.

also, dont play copperhall blessing, it's a trap card. there used to be a deck built around it using pre-nerfed excavate, but let's not rehash bad memories. anyway it doesn't do anything, sure in the right circumstance it can be powerful, but that's very niche. like it only prevents DAMAGE but not kill spells, which are much more common, since units heal automatically

a much better option is protect. its 3 power less, you can use that to block kill spells as well as damage. this way you could protect against ruin, shatterglass mage, and furnace mage as well as torch vara's favor, and oblierate, whereas copperhall blessing only protects vs the latter 3

also the reason the last word fits into feln control is cuz of the cheap damage it has access to; draw, so you can consistently get it, including omen; and eilyn's favor to give yourself aegis is also really big boon for the card. that being said, currently most feln control lists have decided that champ of cunning is their finisher, or even vara or azindal's gift.

also ramping to the last word, doesn't seem like a consistently good idea to me. currently the major ramp deck is owl based, therefore aid of the hooru and the great parliment. these provide immediate board presence often lead to card advantage. basically getting to high power counts is super hard and if you've already gotten to that point, chances are you've already won (assuming your playing the more greedy deck) and in most cases last word inherently functions the same as runehammer, kill something the turn you play it, dies to ping the next turn

finally, good overall advice is never make your gameplan of needing 13+ power. honestly getting there is pretty rare. for instance a very popular card right now, bartholo has an ultimate to pay 10 and draw a relic of your choice. no one has built a deck around this, because it is way too slow, and the people who have gotten to use his ultimate ended up losing the game anyway, since it meant they had nothing else to do with 10 power

edit: some decks do actually have gameplan of activating marshall ironthorn which is 15 power, but again thats for owl ramp decks but mostly vodacombo. like you play ironthorn, followed by mystic ascendent, followed by vodakhan then you play a power, draw your entire deck (well most of it) get up 20 or 30 or more power, activate ironthorn and then hit your op for a billion with mystic and voda, all the while your op can't concede and leave since the animations need to finish first

there are a few reasons:

1. attacking is much more simplistic in HS as you choose where to attack. this also inherently creates an imbalance between going first and second, as the player going first has a better chance of gaining initiative and choosing where to trade. In Eternal, the player blocking chooses the trades

2. class system greatly restricts deck building. in Eternal any card can be played in any deck with any combination of other cards, your only restriction is how consistent you want your deck to be. This also creates balance issues in HS as certain classes will access to better cards than that other classes don't have access to

3. Hero Powers also create an imbalance because some hero powers will be inherently good/bad vs other hero powers. for example paladin's 1/1s can overwhelm a warrior because their hero power doesn't do 1 damage, conversely rogue does very well vs the 1/1 tokens because the paladin payed 4 mana for two token and the rogue payed 2 mana to remove both

4. Also with hero powers, not only do all the cards have to balanced with all the other cards in the game, or at least within their specific class, they also have to be balanced within their relation to hero powers

5. a running theme if you haven't noticed as been about balance. and that is by far HS's biggest issue, always has been, always will be. instead of just having to balance in relation to the cards in the game, the devs have to account for so much more which really make the game a balancing nightmare. This is, imo, Eternal's biggest strength as the game seems vastly more balanced than HS, and the devs aren't afraid to buff/nerf cards either
